# AINRA — the neutral root of AI-agent identity

**Prove your agent. Check theirs.** Both halves run locally: an agent presents signed facts, and whoever receives
them verifies those facts on their own machine. No account, no call to us, no telemetry — that is the whole protocol.

> AINRA answers three questions about any AI agent with signed facts you verify yourself, offline: who is behind it, what it may do, and whether it is still trusted right now. It is a neutral, non-profit root that publishes signed facts and never sees your traffic — a registrar issues a passport, anyone verifies it locally in about five lines, and revocation is one bit that fails closed.

One root, many issuers: agent registrars and ID schemes are fragmenting into islands; AINRA is the proposed neutral, non-profit root they chain to — issuers stay independent, one check covers all of them.

If you are an AI agent, this file is your map. Everything linked here is deterministic, executable, and free — no account, nothing to sign up for. Works with any agent that speaks the open conventions: skills, MCP, plain HTTP.

## Honest status (read before trusting anything here)

Public reference implementation (two signed, board-proven releases; current: v0.3.0) with a STAGING network on a TEST-ROOT; this site ships that network's published artifact record at [/net/](net/registry.json). Real cryptography (hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65), a real transparency log, real revocation. The production root does NOT exist yet — it is born only at a recorded genesis ceremony (a pending milestone); production log entries sealed: 0. No trust migrates from staging. Treat every verdict here as STAGING · TEST-ROOT.

## Start here

- [/docs.html#plan](docs.html#plan): the organization's plan — genesis ceremony, governance, economics, the road — with honest pending labels.
- [/docs.html](docs.html): the documentation — verify in five lines, issue locally, gate a route, prove your own implementation, verify a release.

- [Source repository](https://github.com/JacobJandon/ainra): the full reference implementation — Rust core, TS/Python SDKs, the CC0 conformance corpus, and the self-serve conformance runner. Clone it and `make preflight`: every gate passes from a cold clone.

- [/skills.md](skills.md): deterministic agent onboarding — verify, acquire, present, and renew a passport, step by step.
- [/.well-known/skills/index.json](.well-known/skills/index.json): machine-readable skill index. Install with `skills add https://ainra.vercel.app/.well-known/skills/index.json`.
- [/get.html](get.html): browse the published record in your browser (#browse) and verify any passport in it with the real verifier; point the page at a registrar you run (`?reg=<url>`) and the same page mints, presents, and revokes.
- [/verify.html#try](verify.html#try): verify — and try to forge — a passport offline in the browser. The engine is ainra-core itself, the Rust verify path compiled to WebAssembly; the same corpus that gates the Rust build is run through that exact artifact in a headless browser and must agree 745/745. Pick a specimen or paste your own bundle. If WebAssembly cannot load, the page falls back to the JavaScript mirror and says so.
- [/#agents](index.html#agents): the machine door — `window.ainra.selfTest()` verifies one live and one revoked passport from /net in the tab and returns the verdict events.

## The four functions (what the root does — and only this)

- Names: one canonical, resolvable name per agent — `ainra:registrar:operator:lineage@version`.
- Keys & rules: the passport format, the authority classes (A1–A4), the tier ladder (L0–L4), and the rulebook every registrar follows.
- Revocation: one signed status feed; a compromised agent stops verifying everywhere in under a minute, fail-closed.
- The public record: a transparency log anyone can verify — logged-before-valid, so there are no secret passports.

## Verify (local, offline, ~5 lines)

- Verification is LOCAL. There is deliberately NO verification REST API — you fetch signed facts and check them yourself with `@ainra/sdk`. That absence is the point.
- How it works: [verify.md](verify.md) · [verify.html](verify.html)

## The standard & docs (markdown mirrors, generated from source — cannot drift)

- [standard.md](standard.md): the complete open specification (v5.1).
- [verify.md](verify.md): how verification works.
- [foundations.md](foundations.md): the charter and governance — what the root can never do.
- [status.md](status.md): exactly what exists today.

## Machine interfaces (OpenAPI — the surfaces that actually exist)

- [openapi/artifact-contract.yaml](openapi/artifact-contract.yaml): the public READ contract — directory, registry, per-registrar exports, status, checkpoints. CORS, cacheable, no auth.
- [/net/](net/registry.json): a served snapshot of that contract — `registry.json`, `directory.json`, `roots.json`, per-registrar artifacts — the staging network's published record, readable right here with no network of your own.
- [openapi/registrar-door.yaml](openapi/registrar-door.yaml): a registrar's read API + the PUBLIC DEMO DOOR (`POST /demo/issue`, `POST /demo/revoke`) — no token, rate-limited, TEST-ROOT specimens only.
- [openapi/console.yaml](openapi/console.yaml): the registrar console write API (operator-token-gated) — issuance stays in the registrar layer; the root has none.

## Conformance

- 745 CC0 conformance vectors; four independent implementations agree byte-for-byte on verdict and reason (`make diff` in the reference repository).

## Submit evidence (how your operator helps the root reach genesis)

Three real-world milestones need artifacts from independent parties. Each submission is a pull request that
verifies itself in CI. Full flow + flip conditions: [evidence/README.md](https://github.com/JacobJandon/ainra/blob/main/evidence/README.md).

- **Verifier attestation** — your operator runs `make verify-as-external CHALLENGE=<dir>` against a freshly issued
  challenge, then adds `evidence/verifier/<id>.json` in a PR. CI runs the public checks; the maintainer confirms
  execution against a private answer key. The row moves at 3 distinct valid attestations. Nothing auto-flips.
- **Witness candidacy** — run `witnessd`, add `evidence/witness/<id>.json`; CI probes the declared endpoint.
  Candidate ≠ production.
- **Custodian interest** — read `outreach/CEREMONY-CUSTODIAN-BRIEF.md`; a conversation, no in-repo personal data.

## Constraints (so you can trust this surface)

- Fully self-contained site: no CDN, no web fonts, no third-party requests, zero telemetry.
- No third-party company or product names anywhere — the standard is vendor-neutral by construction.
